about: The one list of parts for Project Daedalus. The three tables in the page's Parts list section are built from this file, and so is daedalus-bom-jlcpcb.csv (run: python3 make_bom.py). Change a part here, not in the page or the CSV.
price_source: Board parts: JLCPCB's parts library (the price its assembly service charges) at the quantity a batch of 30 uses. Other parts: the listing named in each row.

board.pkg: Module, 18 × 25.5 mm, 28 pads and a ground pad
board.does: The computer and the Bluetooth radio

board.rating: 4.2 V charger for one lithium cell, up to 1 A, 4 to 8 V in
board.does: Charges the battery from USB and drives the two charge lights

board.rating: Cuts off above 4.30 V, below 2.40 V and at about 3 A
board.does: Disconnects the battery if it is over-charged, run flat or shorted

board.rating: 3.3 V out, 500 mA, 6 V in at most, loses 0.12 V at 100 mA
board.does: Makes the 3.3 V supply. The slide switch turns it on and off through its enable pin

board.rating: P-channel MOSFET, 30 V, 4 A, fully on at 2.5 V
board.does: Q1 connects the battery to the system rail when the cable is out. Q2 switches the stick's power off in sleep

board.rating: Schottky diode, 40 V, 1 A, drops 0.6 V at 1 A
board.does: Feeds the system rail from USB while the cable is in

board.rating: Rated 10,000 insertions; four legs through the board
board.does: Charging, and loading firmware
Where the battery lead plugs in
board.note: A copy of JST's S2B-PH-SM4-TB(LF)(SN), which this board was first drawn around (C295747, $0.20). On the day checked JLCPCB had none of the JST part and LCSC had 15; this one had 3,134. Its drawing shows the same pad positions. If the JST part is back in stock, use it.

board.does: On/off. It only tells the regulator to turn on or off, so it carries no power
L1, L2, R2 and R1, in that order along the top edge
Select, Start, Home and BOOT
Status light on GPIO15, under the 2 mm window
board.why: White, so it cannot be mistaken for the red and green charge lights. With R15: (3.3 V − about 2.7 V across the LED) ÷ 1 kΩ ≈ 0.6 mA. That is an eighth of its rated 5 mA, kept low on purpose because it is lit all the time you play; it adds under 2 % to the playing current. If it is too dim through the window on the prototype, a smaller resistor is the fix.

board.does: Charge light: on while charging
board.why: With R13: (5.0 V from USB − about 1.9 V across the LED − 0.3 V across the charger's pin) ÷ 1 kΩ ≈ 2.8 mA.

board.does: Charge light: on when the battery is full
board.why: With R14: (5.0 − about 2.8 − 0.3) ÷ 1 kΩ ≈ 1.9 mA. It is one size larger than the other two (0805, 2.0 × 1.25 mm) because JLCPCB has no Basic green LED in 0603; the 0603 one, KT-0603G (C12624), is Extended and would add a $3.07 fee to the order.

board.does: USB-C pins CC1 and CC2 to ground, one each. They tell the charger a device is attached, so it turns the 5 V on
board.why: 5.1 kΩ is the value the USB-C standard fixes for a device that takes power.

board.does: Sets the charging current (charger pin PROG to ground)
board.why: The charger's datasheet gives the current as 1,100 V ÷ the resistance: 1,100 ÷ 3,000 Ω = 0.37 A, about a third of the 1,200 mAh cell's capacity. The chip itself is only good to about 15 %, so 1 % here is more than enough.

board.does: Battery + to the protection chip's supply pin
board.why: 100 Ω here and 100 nF (C8) are the two values in the XB5353A datasheet's own circuit (figure 1).

board.does: R5: Q1's gate to ground. R6 and R7: pull-ups to 3.3 V on Home (GPIO5) and Start (GPIO7), the two buttons that wake the controller
board.why: R5 pulls Q1's gate down when the cable comes out, which connects the battery; with the cable in it passes 5 V ÷ 100 kΩ = 50 µA, taken from USB. R6 and R7 are there because the chip's built-in pull-ups cannot be relied on while it sleeps; each passes nothing until its button is held, then 33 µA. The other ten buttons use the chip's built-in pull-ups and need no resistor.

board.does: Halve the battery voltage so GPIO6 can measure it: battery + to R8, R8 to the pin, the pin to R9, R9 to ground
board.why: They are connected all the time, so they are made large: 4.2 V ÷ 2 MΩ = 2 µA. Two 1 % parts put the half-way point within 1 %. Resistors this large cannot feed the chip's measuring circuit quickly, which is what C12 is for.

board.does: Pull-ups to 3.3 V. R10: the module's EN pin. R11: GPIO9, the BOOT button. R12: GPIO8, which is also Q2's gate
board.why: 10 kΩ on EN with 1 µF (C6), and 10 kΩ on GPIO8, are the values in Espressif's module datasheet (version 1.4, figure 9-1): 10 kΩ × 1 µF holds the chip in reset for about 10 ms while the supply settles. R12 also keeps Q2 off, and so the stick unpowered, until the firmware pulls GPIO8 low.

board.does: R13: red charge light. R14: green charge light. R15: status light. R16 and R17: in line with the stick's X and Y outputs
board.why: The light currents are worked out under LED1 to LED3. On the stick, 1 kΩ with 100 nF (C10, C11) lets through anything slower than 1 ÷ (2π × 1 kΩ × 100 nF) ≈ 1.6 kHz and settles in about half a millisecond, inside the 1 ms between readings, and the capacitor gives the chip's measuring circuit the steady source it wants.

board.does: C1: USB 5 V, at the charger's input. C2: battery +, at the charger's output. C3: regulator input. C4: regulator output
board.why: The charger's datasheet asks for 10 µF at the battery. The regulator's is tested with 1 µF in and 1 µF out; 10 µF is used so the supply holds up when the radio sends. The 10 V rating is twice the 5 V on the cable. A capacitor this small keeps only about half its value at 5 V, which still leaves several times what the regulator needs.

board.does: Reservoir within 3 mm of the module's 3V3 pin, for the radio's bursts
board.why: 22 µF with 100 nF (C7) beside the 3V3 pin is what Espressif's module datasheet draws (version 1.4, figure 9-1). 6.3 V is nearly twice the 3.3 V it sees.

board.does: The module's EN pin to ground: with R10, holds the chip in reset for a moment at power-on
C7: the module's 3V3 pin. C8: the protection chip's supply pin. C9: the stick's supply, after Q2. C10 and C11: stick X and Y at GPIO2 and GPIO3. C12: the battery-sense pin, GPIO6
board.why: C7 and C8 are their chips' datasheet values. C9 steadies the stick's supply at the far end of its track. C10 to C12 each sit right at a measuring pin; see R8 and R16.

hand.buy: This plan's board, 108 × 46 × 1.2 mm, two layers, gold (ENIG) finish, with the 50 parts above soldered on
hand.pack: One order of 30 boards, all assembled. No spares: the two prototype boards are the spares

hand.buy: YTL YHE-YG13-013 SH3B166A5: Hall sensors, 13 mm body, 4 mm D-shaped shaft, click switch, 14 pins through the board
hand.pack: Sold singly. 3 spare, for a lifted pad or a cooked sensor. 460 in stock

hand.buy: PlayStation 4 style replacement thumbstick cap, for a 4 mm D-shaped shaft
hand.confirm: Price seen in a search result only, and the fit on this stick's shaft is not confirmed. Buy one pack with the prototype sticks and try it

hand.buy: Lithium-polymer cell, size 603450 (6 × 34 × 50 mm, up to 52 mm long with its protection board), 3.7 V, 1,200 mAh, with a protection board and a JST-PH 2.0 mm 2-pin plug on a lead of 30 mm or more
hand.where: AliExpress or Amazon sellers; PMD Way
hand.pack: 2 spare. All from one listing. PMD Way sells packs of ten, so 40 there
hand.confirm: $3 is from search results only. $7.41 (PMD Way, pack of ten) is the cheapest price read from a listing; that listing does not say whether a protection board is fitted. The lead length is worked out from the layout, not measured

hand.buy: Replacement silicone pad set for a Super Nintendo (SNES) controller. Only the four-button pad from the set is used
hand.pack: Sold by the set. 3 spare. All from one seller, after measuring a sample

hand.buy: M2 × 0.4 heat-set insert: 3.0 mm long, 3.6 mm outer diameter, for a 3.2 mm hole (CNC Kitchen's "M2 short")
hand.fit: The case's posts are 6.4 mm across with a 3.2 mm hole 4.5 mm deep. That leaves a 1.6 mm wall round the insert; a distributor's listing gives 1.3 mm as the least this insert needs.

hand.buy: M2 × 0.4, 8 mm long, socket head cap screw, ISO 4762 (DIN 912), A2 stainless: head 3.8 mm across and 2.0 mm high, turned with a 1.5 mm hex key
hand.confirm: No price could be read from a listing. About $10 a hundred from marketplace sellers; a search result showed $44.99 a hundred at Zoro
hand.fit: From the head's seat the screw passes 3.5 mm of back shell and the 1.2 mm board, so 3.3 mm of it enters the insert's hole: the whole 3.0 mm insert, with 1.2 mm of the hole to spare.

hand.buy: The same screw, 6 mm long: M2 × 0.4 × 6, socket head cap, ISO 4762, A2 stainless
hand.confirm: Price as for the 8 mm screw
hand.fit: There is no board between the shells at the grips, so an 8 mm screw would reach 4.5 mm into a hole that is 4.5 mm deep and could bottom out before the shells close. A 6 mm screw goes 2.5 mm into the 3.0 mm insert and leaves 2 mm clear. Worked out from the case model; not yet tried on a print.

hand.buy: Double-sided foam tape, 0.5 mm thick (0.6 mm at most), 15 to 20 mm wide
hand.per: 80 mm: two 40 mm strips under the battery
hand.confirm: No listing confirmed at this thickness. The pocket allows 0.6 mm; the common thin foam tape, tesa 62934, is 0.8 mm, which would leave 1.2 mm above the cell where 1.4 mm is drawn

hand.buy: PETG, 1.75 mm, any one colour for the whole batch
hand.per: 75 g: 58 g in the 13 printed pieces, the rest supports
hand.pack: 2.25 kg for 30 cases; the rest covers the test coupons and about 8 spare or failed cases

hand.buy: Clear 5-minute epoxy, or clear UV-curing resin
hand.per: One drop, in the 2 mm hole over the status light

tools.note: Borrow one, or use a school or library printer

tools.confirm: Price is a guess. Many packs of socket screws include one

Cutting leads and supports: the offcuts fly

tools.for: A joint that will not flow
